# XrealImageTracking

**Inherits:** [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)  
**Scene:** `addons/godot_xreal/features/xreal_image_tracking.tscn`  
**Script:** `addons/godot_xreal/features/xreal_image_tracking.gd`  

> The script declares no `class_name`, so **XrealImageTracking** is this reference's name for it, not a type you can write in GDScript. Use it by instancing `addons/godot_xreal/features/xreal_image_tracking.tscn`.

Image tracking as a drop-in feature component (Air 2 Ultra). On first enable it loads EVERY set in the manifest JSON (each set = one blob built by scripts/build_image_db.* / the editor dock), builds a database per set (XrealSystem.init_image_database), activates the first, and overlays a world-locked quad on each tracked image. cycle_set() switches the active set. Point `manifest_path` at a reference.json (see demo/image_tracking/reference.json for the schema): top-level `sets[]`, each {name, blob, images:[{guid, width, height?}]} with blob paths relative to the manifest.

World-locked: add this component under a world-fixed node (e.g. the scene root, NOT the head rig) so a marker sits on the real image as the head moves. OFF hides the markers but keeps the databases active so ON restores them.

## Properties

<a id="property-enabled"></a>

### enabled: bool = false

Enable at boot (applied in _ready). At runtime call set_enabled().

<a id="property-manifest_path"></a>

### manifest_path: String = ""

The reference-image manifest (JSON). Required — set_enabled(true) refuses while empty.

<a id="property-marker_material"></a>

### marker_material: Material

Optional override for the tracked-image overlay material. Each marker gets its own duplicate. A ShaderMaterial declaring a `tracking` bool uniform receives the per-marker tracking state (replacing the default material's green/gray albedo tint).

## Signals

<a id="signal-error"></a>

### error(message: String)

Emitted whenever an operation fails or the feature is unavailable (unbuilt/missing blob, DB init failure, manifest not set…), so the load site can react — show UI, log, flip a toggle. Carries the same human-readable text also pushed as a warning.

<a id="signal-set_changed"></a>

### set_changed(name: String)

Emitted with the active set's name when the active tracking set changes (on load and on cycle_set), so the load site can label a "cycle" button with the current set.

## Methods

<a id="method-cycle_set"></a>

### cycle_set()

Cycle to the next set. No-op with 0/1 set.

<a id="method-set_enabled"></a>

### set_enabled(on: bool) -> bool

Toggle image-tracking mode. Returns the resulting state (false if the ABI / manifest / blobs are unavailable, so a UI toggle can flip itself back off).
